propositions: Plan-review grounding finders (G1G2/E4/E6) flag symbols as missing even when a prerequisite ticket will create them, because they only check the origin/main snapshot and ignore depends_on prerequisites.
The existing documentation claims symbols from depends_on tickets should be treated as existing, but this rule is unimplemented in the code.

Cited prerequisites with verified edges must be checked via a two-layer system: Layer 1 deterministically parses [rebar:<id>] tokens and verifies the edge (both directions: depends_on or blocks), then Layer 2 uses LLM judgment to confirm the cited ticket actually provides the claimed functionality.

Layer 1 edge verification must accept both upstream encodings: the plan's own depends_on relation to the cited ticket, or the cited ticket's blocks relation back to the plan (reverse lookup via injected resolve_deps callable).

A citation lacking a verified edge, or one where the cited ticket does not cover the claimed functionality, must not suppress the missing-symbol finding (fail-closed; never block at the advisory layer).

The reverse-lookup and coverage judgment must gracefully handle failures without propagating exceptions, treating lookup errors as unverified citations and deferring to the normal missing-symbol block.
